item.title: US Democratic congressional candidate Lander detained by Israeli authorities in West Bank
item.description: Brad Lander, a US Democratic Party candidate for Congress, was detained by Israeli forces in the occupied West Bank on Wednesday, along with other Americans, Israelis and Palestinians taking part in the annual olive harvest, rights groups said.
item.dc:creator: Alexander Cornwell
item.content:encoded: Brad Lander, a US Democratic Party candidate for Congress, was detained by Israeli forces in the occupied West Bank on Wednesday, along with other Americans, Israelis and Palestinians taking part in the annual olive harvest, rights groups said. The incident took place in Nahalin, a village south of Bethlehem, as Palestinians were gathering olives accompanied by around 80 volunteers, according to Israeli organisation Rabbis for Human Rights and Jewish North American organisation T'ruah. Lander, a Jewish American and former New York City comptroller and mayoral candidate, wrote on X that he had been detained along with a group of rabbis and volunteers. "We were simply harvesting olives in a grove near Nahalin in the West Bank. The occupation is a crime under international law. Harvesting olives isn't a crime under any law I know." Lander, who is an ally of New York Mayor Zohran Mamdani and has been critical of Israel's conduct in the war in Gaza , was later released, according to Rabbis for Human Rights and T'ruah. Lander, who is running for New York's 10th Congressional District in the US House of Representatives in the November 3 midterm elections , was not immediately available for comment. Israeli police said it had detained Palestinian olive harvesters and dozens of Israeli and foreign activists gathering olives near the fence of an Israeli settlement, saying it was prohibited. One of the foreign nationals was later released once it became known he was a congressional candidate, police said. The military said harvesting in that area required prior coordination, which had not happened, and that those present had been detained. It did not say harvesting there was prohibited. Lander is the only one released so far, while the others are expected to be interrogated, according to Rabbis for Human Rights Acting Director Anton Goodman. "I would suggest to all activists go out there and get yourself elected," he said. HARVEST AREA DECLARED A CLOSED MILITARY ZONE The volunteers were accompanying local farmers gathering olives who often are faced with the threat of violence from Israeli settlers, as an act of solidarity in what is known as protective presence. Israeli settler violence against Palestinians is surging, while the Israeli military continues to curb Palestinian freedoms, including access to farmland. Olives are the backbone of Palestinian agriculture, a sector that accounts for around 8% of GDP and more than 60,000 jobs, according to the Palestinian Authority's agriculture ministry. Rabbis for Human Rights and T'ruah said Israeli military and police forces arrived around two hours after the Palestinians and volunteers began gathering olives, and informed them that they were in a closed military zone and would be detained. Goodman said they were not aware the area had been declared a closed military zone since it had only been issued that morning but they told the Israeli forces they would respect the order and leave. "However, we were told that we cannot leave because we have been disturbing the public order," he said by phone, speaking from a police station in the Israeli Betar Illit settlement. "If you would have come to our harvest earlier today, you would have found a place that was quiet and peaceful and respectful and definitely not harming any of the public order." Among those detained were over 30 US citizens, as well as UK and Canadian citizens, according to Rabbi Jill Jacobs, chief executive of T'ruah, who is among those who have been detained. "We were obviously not doing anything violent but just the very act of picking olives together with Palestinian farmers was apparently disturbing for some," Jacobs, a 51-year-old rabbi from Manhattan, told Reuters by phone. A spokesperson for the US Embassy in Jerusalem said it was aware of reports that US citizens had been detained and was monitoring the situation but declined further comment, citing privacy and other considerations. "The Trump administration has no higher priority than the safety and security of Americans," he said. Israeli settler attacks against Palestinians and other civilians in the West Bank over the weekend prompted a call by US Secretary of State Marco Rubio on Saturday for Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's government to [USN:SPN45V01F TEXT:"crack down"] on the violence. An American photojournalist for the Washington Post covering a Palestinian olive harvest on Friday was [USN:L8N4620II TEXT:"beaten"] by Israeli settlers, while European diplomats and a French mayor were [USN:L8N46405A TEXT:"attacked"] at another Palestinian olive harvest by settlers on Saturday. Palestinians were attacked by settlers in both incidents. Israeli police announced on [USN:S8N43804R TEXT:"Monday"] it had made 10 arrests in connection with the weekend violence. (This story has been corrected to change the day of the Israeli announcement of arrests to Monday, not Tuesday, in paragraph 26.)

item.title: South Africa need six wickets after Australia follow on to level test series
item.description: South Africa need six more wickets to complete a remarkable turnaround and win the second test against Australia, who were forced to follow on after being dismissed for 99 in their first innings on the fourth day at St George’s Park in Gqeberha on Wednesday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: South Africa need six more wickets to complete a remarkable turnaround and win the second test against Australia, who were forced to follow on after being dismissed for 99 in their first innings on the fourth day at St George’s Park in Gqeberha on Wednesday. Australia were 156-4 in their second innings at close of play, still trailing by 170 runs after making a better fight of it than they had when crumbling under the South African attack earlier in the day. But they were still facing an uphill task despite Travis Head edging close to a century. He will resume on 87 on the final day alongside nightwatchman Scott Boland, who is on two. It was a day of tumbling wickets as Australia, resuming on 3-1, were skittled out for 99 an hour after lunch, leaving them with a 326-run deficit after South Africa had scored 425–9 declared in the first innings. Lanky fast bowler Marco Jansen took 5-33 in 11 overs as he ripped through the tourists, who posted their fourth-lowest total against South Africa. Wiaan Mulder (2-14), Kagiso Rabada (2-33) and Anrich Nortje (1-5) took the other wickets, but Nortje only bowled 3.3 overs before a groin injury forced him off the field and out of the day’s play, leaving South Africa one bowler short as they put Australia in to bat again. Sharp catching from South Africa contributed to Australia’s first innings collapse, with Simon Harmer taking three in the innings – the best a diving one-handed effort in the slips to dismiss Marnus Labuschagne. It should have been a celebratory day for veteran Steve Smith, who reached the milestone of 11,000 test runs as he top-scored with 28 in the first innings, but he struggled with a neck injury and did not come out to bat in the second innings, dropping down the order as he continued his treatment. Australia’s second innings began in almost the same manner as the first had, with Nic Maddinson out early, edging Rabada to wicketkeeper Ryan Rickelton for eight runs. But a 92-run partnership for the second wicket between Head and Labuschagne took Australia past their first innings total as South Africa’s attack began to tire. However, an injudicious attempt to hammer spinner Harmer over the top saw Labuschagne caught near the boundary for 39 and he was followed by Matt Renshaw, hero of Australia’s 214-run victory in last week’s opening test in Durban, who was bowled by Rabada for 11. Beau Webster (8) was the 13th Australian wicket of the day as Harmer trapped him lbw, exposing the tail on the final day. The first two days of the test were largely washed out, but South Africa staged a major fightback on Tuesday after being 110-6 with captain Temba Bavuma turning the match on its head with a majestic 179-run knock.

Oct 21 : South Korean entertainment platform Korai Flix will go public in the U.S. through a $3.5 billion merger with special purpose acquisition company APEX Tech Acquisition, the companies said on Wednesday. The deal comes as SPACs, an alternative route to public markets, are making a comeback in the US after years of subdued activity. Korai's platform, launched in 2024, offers AI-generated short dramas and AI companion avatars to roughly 26 million users across 15 countries in Asia. Users can also use tools to create such content in various visual styles. Microdramas, short episodic vertical videos delivered in two-minute episodes for viewing on phones, have surged in popularity worldwide. The format is cheap to produce and can be generated rapidly using artificial intelligence.

In the first half of 2026, microdramas on YouTube garnered more than 6.5 billion views, while watch time grew over 50 per cent from a year earlier. Korean entertainment content is also flourishing across the world following the success of K-pop, K-dramas and other Korean cultural exports. Korai will be the latest South Korea-linked entertainment platform to go public in US. Naver-backed Webtoon Entertainment, which owns novel distribution platform Wattpad, debuted in New York in 2024 through a traditional IPO. A SPAC is a shell company that raises capital through an initial public offering and then uses the funds to merge with or acquire a private company, taking it public without a traditional IPO. The SPAC deal is expected to close in the first quarter of 2027. The combined company will be renamed Krflix Group and is expected to list on the New York Stock Exchange.

Source: Reuters

item.title: UK's FTSE 100 ticks higher on energy boost; hot inflation report limits gains
item.description: Britain's FTSE 100 edged higher on Wednesday, supported by gains in oil majors and financial stocks, though hotter-than-expected inflation reinforced expectations of a Bank of England interest rate hike, limiting the index's upside.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Britain's FTSE 100 edged higher on Wednesday, supported by gains in oil majors and financial stocks, though hotter-than-expected inflation reinforced expectations of a Bank of England interest rate hike, limiting the index's upside. The blue-chip FTSE 100 index (.FTSE) rose 0.1% to 10,752.88 points, after two sessions of declines in a row. The midcap FTSE 250 (.FTMC) was up 0.3%. [USN:L8N46708O TEXT:"UK inflation"] rose to 3.5% in September, above economists' expectations of 3.4%, as the US-Israeli war on Iran pushed up energy prices Money markets are near certain of a 25-basis-point BoE rate hike in November, according to LSEG data Finance Minister John Healey came under pressure ahead of next week's budget after official data showed government borrowing exceeded forecasts for a second straight month, pushing [USN:L8N46708T TEXT:"public debt above £3 trillion"] ($4.01 trillion) "Widespread expectations of relatively stable economic policy and a market-friendly budget limit the upside for the FTSE 100, particularly if such a budget were to manifest itself primarily in a stronger GBP," Duncan Toms, multi-asset strategist at HSBC, said in a note, reiterating a neutral stance on UK stocks Energy giants gained, with BP (BP.L) and Shell (SHEL.L) among the biggest boosts to the FTSE 100 Britain [USN:L8N46707X TEXT:"approved "]the Jackdaw North Sea gas field, ending years of legal and political wrangling as the Labour government seeks to balance its climate goals with energy security concerns Asset manager Aberdeen Group (ABDN.L) , among the top losers on the FTSE 100, fell 4% after flagging a [USN:L6N4670H8 TEXT:"slower-than-expected return"] to adviser-segment inflows Midcaps: bicycles-to-car parts retailer Halfords (HFD.L) dropped about 8.6%, the steepest on the FTSE 250, after [USN:L4N4670KL TEXT:"first-half results"]

item.title: Jio Platforms' IPO-linked inflows boost rupee; elevated oil prices spur caution
item.description: The Indian rupee experienced a notable increase as Jio Platforms' IPO attracted significant foreign investments. Despite this strength, rising oil prices raised concerns among traders about the rupee's sustainability. The rupee closed at 94.46 against the dollar, with earlier gains trimmed by higher Brent crude oil prices. Analysts suggest that the upcoming RBI monetary policy might influence future exchange rates.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: The Indian rupee strengthened sharply on Wednesday, helped along by foreign portfolio inflows linked to Jio Platforms' IPO while persistently elevated oil prices kept traders cautious about positioning for further gains in the unit.The rupee closed up 0.5% at 94.46 against the dollar after touching a peak of 94.43 earlier in the day, its strongest level since early September.It trimmed gains in the latter half of the session as oil prices rose and local stocks fell. Brent crude oil futures were last up 1.3% at over $110 per barrel while India's benchmark equity index, the Nifty 50, declined 0.7%.Escalating Middle East tensions fuelled fears of supply disruptions, lifting oil prices after Iran told Pakistan's army chief there would be no talks with Washington until its demands were met. Volatility in oil will keep rupee a little on the defensive but sharp falls are unlikely in the near term, a trader at a state-run lender said.Despite the global headwinds, inflows linked to Jio Platforms' $3.2 billion IPO aided the rupee. The IPO was fully subscribed in less than two hours of public bidding on Wednesday as investors flocked to India's largest share sale. With USD/INR holding below 95.00, focus shifts to 94.80-94.70. A sustained break below 94.80 could open the way towards 94.00 over the coming weeks, keeping the near-term outlook favourable for the rupee, said Amit Pabari, managing director at FX advisory firm CR Forex.Elsewhere, Asian currencies were mostly rangebound and the dollar index was little changed at 101.8.Focus will now turn to the release of the minutes of the RBI's latest monetary policy review held earlier this month. The central bank had delivered its first rate hike in four years on October 7 and signalled more were likely to come.Data released last week showed that India's retail inflation accelerated to a higher-than-expected 5.54% in September.Swap markets are currently pricing in over 100 bps of rate hikes by the RBI over the next 12 months.

item.title: Wall St sees Tesla-SpaceX merger as inevitable, but split on price
item.description: A Tesla-SpaceX merger appears to be a matter of when, not if, to many on Wall Street. But they disagree on a key factor: how much Tesla shareholders should be paid.
item.dc:creator: Akash Sriram
item.content:encoded: A Tesla-SpaceX merger appears to be a matter of when, not if, to many on Wall Street. But they disagree on a key factor: how much Tesla shareholders should be paid. That tension runs through [USN:L4N4661M0 TEXT:"a deal"] where predictions on the premium Tesla shareholders would get to swap into a stock of SpaceX (SPCX.O) that Elon Musk controls run from little or none to 35%. With Tesla (TSLA.O) worth about $1.5 trillion, the premium could run into hundreds of billions of dollars, making it a major swing factor in any deal. The billionaire, a self-described 'conflicted party', said the committees are [USN:L1N46701K TEXT:"yet to agree"] on terms, even as Wall Street sees a deal being proposed in the coming months. Tesla shares gained more than 3%, while SpaceX rose 11% on Wednesday and was set to add about $210 billion to its market capitalization if gains hold, roughly equal to that of CitiGroup (C.N) . SpaceX and Tesla are jointly developing the Terafab chip plant, and AI now makes up more than half of SpaceX's revenue, with another $35 billion to $40 billion spending likely in fourth quarter to fund further expansion. "(A Tesla-SpaceX merger) is very strategic as both companies are [USN:L6N43O1D8 TEXT:"rapidly transitioning"] into artificial intelligence and autonomous systems, and both have huge infrastructure projects underway," said Justus Parmar, CEO of Fortuna Investments and an investor in both companies. "It would also avoid redundancy and the time he spends going back and forth between two entities, and there would be a reduction in public company overhead, legal costs and administrative burdens." Analysts have said that [USN:L6N46211S TEXT:"burgeoning capital spending"] for expensive AI and space infrastructure would weigh on SpaceX's free cash flow, a strain a combined company could ease by sharing services and borrowing jointly with Tesla. They also pointed to last week's [USN:L1N46200L TEXT:"Roadster unveiling"], where a Tesla car built with SpaceX rocket thrusters flipped and leapt over vehicles, as a teaser for what a combined company could produce. However, much of the technology on which the lofty valuations of the companies are based, including data centers in orbit, self-driving taxis at scale and humanoid robots, has yet to reach commercial scale. That would take years of heavy spending and engineering, adding execution risk to a deal already facing questions over governance and price. "The big reason why this makes so much sense is that what Tesla is doing SpaceX needs and what SpaceX is doing Tesla needs," Gene Munster, managing partner at Tesla investor Deepwater Asset Management, said on X. "And both of them operate under the grand vision which is Elon building a true vertical AI company." PREMIUM - THE NEXT BATTLE Price is likely to be the next fight. Tesla shareholders would be swapping a stake in an independent company, where Musk holds about 20% of the vote, for shares in SpaceX that Musk controls. RBC Capital Markets and JPMorgan analysts expect investors would want a premium of between 20% and 35%, but some do not expect a premium. Ross Gerber, CEO of Gerber Kawasaki, whose firm owns both stocks, argues that any premium would dilute SpaceX shareholders as its spending bills rise. Michael Monaghan of Founder ETFs said the overlap between the two shareholder bases means he does not expect a substantial premium. TESLA VOTE IS THE HURDLE Control may also be part of Musk's appeal for a merger. Musk holds about 85% of SpaceX's voting power through super-voting shares. But at Tesla he has roughly 20%. Bill Birmingham, head of research at REX Financial, estimates a merger would give the billionaire about 57% of voting rights. Ryan Zurrer, founder of Dialectic, puts it at 58% at an exchange ratio of 0.7 of one SpaceX share, the illustrative level Barclays has floated. No ratio has been negotiated. Zurrer said a ratio near 0.6 would be needed for Musk to keep control if he sold more equity, and that "the biggest hurdle will be the Tesla shareholders vote vs Elon's own incentives". Musk said Tesla side needs a majority of all shares, not just those voted, so every uncast ballot counts against a deal. Analysts have flagged turnout as a risk, citing uncast broker votes at last year's meeting as a potential factor that could affect chances of a deal going through. Governance and regulatory questions would follow. When Tesla bought SolarCity in 2016, a Delaware court cleared it after years of litigation but said it should have formed an independent committee. "A deal where one man runs both sides will draw tough questions on governance," said Josh Gilbert, lead analyst for APAC at eToro. Tesla is set to report third-quarter results after markets close. Analysts said they were also watching out for disclosures of merger talks in regulatory filings ahead of the automaker's December 3 annual shareholder meeting.

item.title: AT&T's fiber revenue per user to keep sliding as bundle discounts weigh
item.description: AT&T expects average revenue per fiber customer to extend its third-quarter decline into the fourth, as more customers sign up for discounted bundles, suggesting its subscriber-growth strategy is coming at the cost of lower spending per user.
item.dc:creator: Harshita Varghese
item.content:encoded: AT&T (T.N) expects average revenue per fiber customer to extend its third-quarter decline into the fourth, as more customers sign up for discounted bundles, suggesting its subscriber-growth strategy is coming at the cost of lower spending per user. The company's shares fell 6.5% on Wednesday, while rivals T-Mobile (TMUS.O) and Verizon (VZ.N) dropped about 3%. Bundling broadband plans with wireless services and heavy discounts is seen as a critical move by US telecom carriers as a way to attract and retain customers in a competitive market. About 43% of households signing up for AT&T's internet services also opted for its wireless plans. CEO John Stankey said AT&T had "every reason to believe that a converged customer that's sitting on fiber is going to be a sticky and high lifetime value customer." The broader telecom industry is banking on customer loyalty amid concerns that SpaceX's plans to [USN:L6N45U1AK TEXT:"build"] a terrestrial wireless network could intensify competition. AT&T has made significant investments in expanding its fiber network, including through its $5.75 billion acquisition of Lumen's consumer fiber business in 2025. MoffettNathanson analysts said AT&T's recent price increases for fiber internet suggest the company may have concluded that "discounting doesn't drive enough incremental volume to be worthwhile." Average revenue per user across AT&T's fiber base fell 4% in the third quarter, reflecting discounts, introductory pricing in new markets and the addition of lower-priced Lumen customers. During the quarter, AT&T added 379,000 net monthly bill-paying wireless subscribers, compared with 379,300 additions estimated by FactSet. AT&T beat quarterly revenue and profit estimates and lifted its annual adjusted profit forecast to about $2.40 per share, up from a prior range of $2.25 to $2.35.

item.title: Nasdaq climbs over 1% as SpaceX, Super Micro improve AI sentiment
item.description: The tech-heavy Nasdaq led gains on Wednesday after quarterly results from SpaceX and Super Micro Computer improved appetite for AI-linked stocks, while Netflix slipped as its forecast failed to impress investors.
item.dc:creator: Purvi Agarwal, Tharuniyaa Lakshmi
item.content:encoded: The tech-heavy Nasdaq led gains on Wednesday after quarterly results from SpaceX and Super Micro Computer improved appetite for AI-linked stocks, while Netflix slipped as its forecast failed to impress investors. Elon Musk's rocket and space technology firm (SPCX.O) rose 9.8% after he said on Tuesday that [USN:L4N4661M0 TEXT:"a merger of SpaceX"] and Tesla (TSLA.O) would be "a good idea". SpaceX also posted its first profit as a public company. Tesla shares were up 3.5%. Super Micro (SMCI.O) jumped 10.3% to the top of the S&P 500 after the AI server maker [USN:L4N4661QH TEXT:"forecast"] quarterly revenue and profit margin above Wall Street estimates, signaling that AI demand remained resilient. Peers HPE (HPE.N) and Dell (DELL.N) rose 2.2% and 4.5%, respectively. Investors drew comfort from the reports as concerns over the profitability of the AI buildout triggered a selloff in AI-linked stocks last week, with data center operator CoreWeave (CRWV.O) at the center of the storm. Its shares were marginally down, suggesting lingering caution in the sector. "The sentiment around tech has shifted ... There's a lot of stress in the credit markets right now that is keeping a lid on breakouts in tech," said Mark Hackett, chief market strategist for Nationwide. "Most people are just going to wait and see the whites of the eyes of that (next week's tech) earnings because the skepticism is very high right now, both in terms of sustainability of the buildout and the quality of the companies themselves." At 11:36 a.m. ET, the Dow Jones Industrial Average (.DJI) rose 132.16 points, or 0.25%, to 52,628.04, the S&P 500 (.SPX) gained 35.56 points, or 0.46%, to 7,748.13 and the Nasdaq Composite (.IXIC) gained 276.30 points, or 1.05%, to 26,701.12. The S&P 500 information technology sector (.SPLRCT) rose 1.3%, lifting the benchmark index, as most chip stocks rebounded. The Philadelphia SE Semiconductor index (.SOX) was up 1.3%. The index has had a volatile month so far, during which it declined for eight consecutive sessions, marking its longest losing streak in 18 years. The overall rise on the S&P 500 was contained by a 1.2% drop in communication services stocks (.SPLRCL) , dragged down by a 6.3% slide in telecom operator AT&T (T.N) despite beating [USN:L4N4670UN TEXT:"third-quarter"] revenue and profit estimates. Netflix (NFLX.O) slipped 1.8% after the streaming giant issued [USN:L6N4661BU TEXT:"a weaker-than-expected forecast"] for its fourth-quarter profit. Google parent Alphabet (GOOGL.O) also lost 1.9%. Investors are sharply scrutinizing corporate earnings, especially from AI-aligned companies, for clues on whether the AI spending cycle is sustainable and the impact from rising oil prices. Meta (META.O) and Tesla are scheduled to report after markets close. Meanwhile, oil prices remained elevated, with Brent crude futures trading near $110 a barrel. Data last week confirmed that price pressures were seeping into the US economy, and had broadened beyond energy products, supporting the case for another interest rate hike by the Federal Reserve. However, markets largely expect the central bank to remain on hold. Abbott Laboratories (ABT.N) fell 4.3% after the medical device maker cut its [USN:L4N4670ZJ TEXT:"2026 sales growth forecast"]. Advancing issues outnumbered decliners by a 1.46-to-1 ratio on the NYSE and by a 1.51-to-1 ratio on the Nasdaq. The S&P 500 posted 19 new 52-week highs and 2 new lows, while the Nasdaq Composite recorded 39 new highs and 133 new lows.

item.title: プーチン氏、米国人元教師を解放と表明 トランプ氏の要請受け
item.description: [モスクワ ２１日 ロイター] -
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
[モスクワ　２１日　ロイター] - ロシアのプーチン大統領は２１日、２０２２年から同国で拘束されていた元教師の米国人スティーブン・ハバード氏（７４）が解放され、サンクトペテルブルクのプルコボ空港に移送されたと明らかにした。ミシガン州出身のハバード氏は、非公開の裁判で雇い兵活動を行ったとして有罪判決を受け、ロシアで７年近くの刑に服していた。

プーチン氏は、サンクトペテルブルクでトランプ米政権のウィットコフ中東担当特使と会談した際にこの発表を行ったものの、それ以上の詳細は明らかにしなかった。ロシアのペスコフ大統領報道官は後に、プーチン氏がトランプ米大統領の要請を受けてハバード氏を解放したと述べ、同氏の健康状態も考慮したと説明した。

国営テレビで放映された会談で、ウィットコフ氏はプーチン氏に対し「（トランプ）大統領も、国民全体も、ハバード氏の件について感謝の意を示している」とし、「あなたのおかげで彼は家族の元に帰ることができる」と述べた。

ロイターに提供された動画には、ウィットコフ氏とロシア側交渉担当のドミトリエフ氏が、非公開の場所でハバード氏と対面する様子が映っていた。ハバード氏はウィットコフ氏と握手し、「尽力に深く感謝する」と語った。

トランプ氏は自身の交流サイト（ＳＮＳ）「トゥルース・ソーシャル」への投稿で、ハバード氏の解放を確認。その上で、「米国はトランプ大統領への敬意から、何も見返りを提供する必要がなかった。これはロシアにとって前例のない状況だ。今回の解放に『交換』は必要なかった。この重要な帰還は本来、ロシア大統領府との交渉で何も得られなかったバイデン前政権下でもっと早くに実現されるべきだった」と記した。

ハバード氏は２２年４月、ウクライナ東部のイジューム市で逮捕された。ロシア検察当局は、同氏が同地でウクライナ軍の検問所の警備にあたっていたと主張していた。

ロシア国営メディアは、ハバード氏が起訴内容について有罪を認めたと報じた。しかし、米国を拠点とする同氏の弁護士マーティン・デ・ルカ氏は以前、ロイターに対し、ハバード氏から「自分に対する罪状は虚偽であり、いかなる戦闘部隊や軍事部隊にも所属していなかった」と伝えられていたことを明らかにしている。

item.title: Colombia to enact 2027 budget by decree after congressional process fails
item.description: Colombia's government said on Wednesday it will enact its 2027 budget of 634.9 trillion pesos ($198.83 billion) by decree after a procedural error in Congress derailed final approval of the bill, testing the new administration's ability to manage public finances and reassure investors.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Colombia's government said on Wednesday it will enact its 2027 budget of 634.9 trillion pesos ($198.83 billion) by decree after a procedural error in Congress derailed final approval of the bill, testing the new administration's ability to manage public finances and reassure investors. The Senate and lower chamber [USN:L6N4660ZT TEXT:"passed different versions"] of the budget bill earlier this week without reconciling the changes, causing lawmakers and legal experts to argue the process was invalid. Vice President Jose Manuel Restrepo said the government's original proposal, together with the amendments previously approved by lawmakers, will now take effect The Senate approved the bill on Monday night and the lower house passed it early Tuesday, but a disputed article was approved with different wording in each chamber and never went through the required conciliation process Colombia is facing widening fiscal pressures - the 2027 spending plan is larger than the 2026 budget of 555.8 trillion pesos and projects a fiscal deficit of 9.4% of gross domestic product ($1 = 3,193.1200 Colombian pesos)

item.title: France's Macron vows order, calls foreign criticism of unrest 'stupid'
item.description: President Emmanuel Macron vowed on Wednesday to prevent a repeat of last weekend's violence at protests planned in the coming days, and dismissed as "stupid" and "unacceptable" comments from some foreign leaders about the unrest.
item.dc:creator: Elizabeth Pineau, Dominique Patton
item.content:encoded: President Emmanuel Macron vowed on Wednesday to prevent a repeat of [USN:L1N46401W TEXT:"last weekend's"] violence at protests planned in the coming days, and dismissed as "stupid" and "unacceptable" comments from some foreign leaders about the unrest. France's main student union, UNEF, has called for further rallies on Saturday, while the Yellow Vest group, which emerged as a potent anti-establishment movement in 2018, has filed plans for a march through central Paris the same day. Efforts to ease social tensions showed little sign of progress, as unions pledged to press ahead with a general strike on November 5 to denounce the high cost of living and cuts to public services after government talks ended inconclusively. France was hit by some of the worst urban tumult in years on October 17 on the fringe of nationwide protests, shocking the nation both because of its scale and the apparent inability of police to contain it. Macron said he would meet intelligence officials and senior ministers on Thursday to discuss the crisis. "Those who want to cause disorder in city centres next Saturday will be prevented from doing so," Macron told reporters during a visit to Qatar, where he has been seeking energy deals as France grapples with rising fuel costs. He also accused some foreign leaders of spreading misinformation about what had happened. US President Donald Trump in particular [USN:L1N46602Q TEXT:"has blamed"] immigrants and radical Islam, without providing evidence, and said the turbulence was a warning for Americans. Asked whether he was referring to Trump, Macron said: "Among others", adding that some foreign politicians were looking to make political capital at the expense of France. "There was foreign disinformation in the aftermath, which prompted comments that were as unacceptable as they were stupid from many people, including foreign leaders," he said. BORROWING COSTS RISE AS INVESTORS FRET Highlighting investor concern over the situation, French government borrowing costs have jumped this week, pushing benchmark 10-year bond yields to 5%, [USN:L8N4670MT TEXT:"their highest level"] since July 2002. Analysts said the move reflected worries that the unrest could complicate government efforts to repair strained public finances at a time of already mounting budget pressures. Prime Minister Sebastien Lecornu met union leaders in an effort to defuse the crisis, but there was no sign of a breakthrough, with labour groups saying they had received no concrete response to their demands on wages and public services. "There has been no consideration whatsoever of our demands," said Sophie Binet, head of the left-wing CGT group. "The time has come to take the mobilisation to the next level," she added, confirming next month's national strike. The protests reflect a deeper malaise in France, where high energy costs, pressure on household budgets and concerns about the state of public services have fed a growing sense of frustration among workers and young people. A second consecutive night of local curfews passed without major incidents in areas hit by the mayhem, offering the government some respite as it prepared for fresh demonstrations. Government ministers have promised a vastly reinforced security operation this coming Saturday after acknowledging shortcomings in their initial response, with troops expected to be deployed alongside additional police. Justice Minister Gerald Darmanin said on Wednesday around 2,500 people had been taken into custody following the October 17 protests, adding that 917 suspects had been referred for prosecution and 174 people already jailed. PROTESTS ELSEWHERE IN EUROPE The unrest has triggered a political backlash ahead of presidential elections next year, with candidates from the far right and hard left performing strongly in polls. "The government has lost control of everything," far-right leader Marine Le Pen told Franceinfo radio. The hard-left France Unbowed (LFI), which has denied allegations by ministers of fueling the unrest, criticised plans to deploy troops on the streets of Paris. "Demonstrators are not enemies within. The French government must not go to war against its own people," LFI's parliamentary group said in a statement. Protests in other European countries have added to concerns that anger over living standards risks spreading at a time when many nations are struggling with budget woes. In Greece, thousands of [USN:L6N4660T6 TEXT:"students and teachers"] took to the streets on Wednesday, demanding higher state funding for education, better facilities and less-crowded classrooms, echoing protesters in other European countries. Meanwhile [USN:L8N4661X4 TEXT:"Italy approved"] a raft of security measures on Tuesday, including a new offence of violent participation in a demonstration and tougher penalties for rioters in response to turbulence last weekend.

item.title: 中国・香港株式市場・大引け＝下落、ＣＡＴＬ10％安 景気対策への期待後退
item.description:
Summer Zhen
[香港 ２１日 ロイター] - 中国・香港株式市場は下落。アジア株全般は回復基調にあるものの、...
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
中国・香港株式市場・大引け＝下落、ＣＡＴＬ10％安　景気対策への期待後退 10/21 19:08 配信

Summer Zhen

[香港 ２１日 ロイター] - 中国・香港株式市場は下落。アジア株全般は回復基調にあるものの、寧徳時代新能源科技（ＣＡＴＬ）の利益成長鈍化や、消費喚起に向けた大型景気刺激策への期待後退がセンチメントを圧迫した。

ＣＳＩ３００指数は１％安で引け、２０２５年８月以来の安値となった。上海総合指数は０．６％安。

香港のハンセン指数は０．９％安。

ハンセンテック指数は、中国が市場下支えのために大規模な景気刺激策を導入した２０２４年９月以来の安値に沈んだ。

中国のバッテリー最大手 のＣＡＴＬ株は香港・本土市場ともに１０％超急落。競争激化と中国の自動車販売の伸び鈍化を受け、第３・四半期の利益成長が大幅に減速したと発表した。

玩具メーカー、ポップマートの業績不振もリスク回避姿勢を強めた。株価は２１日に５％下落。第３・四半期決算が失望視されるとと見込まれる中、今月１５％下げている。

市場関係者によると、投資家は第３・四半期の決算発表を前に、消費関連株の売買を通じて中国国内需要の弱さに対する弱気の見方を示している。経済成長が引き続き堅調な中、政策当局が早期に市場刺激策を打ち出す公算は小さいとみられている。

バークレイズはリポートで、輸出主導の産業が堅調なため引き続き内需の弱さを覆い隠していると指摘。「成長目標がほぼ達成されており、大規模な景気刺激策導入のハードルは高まったとみている」との見方を示した。

酒類と新エネルギー関連企業が下げを主導した一方、医薬品、通信、クラウドコンピューティング関連企業は相場をアウトパフォームした。

ジュリアス・ベアのエコノミスト、ソフィー・アルターマット氏はリポートで「政府の焦点は、短期的な成長押し上げよりも、技術進歩、産業の高度化、自給率の一段の向上に引き続き置かれている」と指摘した。

市場関係者によると、短期的にはより厳格な税制政策も株式相場の重しとなっている。

ロイターの報道によると、中国政府は富裕層に対し、海外信託関連の所得税を１０月２２日までに申告・納税するよう求めた。これを受け、現金確保のため株式を売却する動きが一部で広がっている。

小型株中心の深セン総合指数は０．４９％安、新興企業向け市場「創業板（チャイネクスト）」総合指数は１．６２％下落、上海証券取引所の新興ハイテク企業向け市場「科創板」５０指数は０．０６％高。

ロイター 関連ニュース コラム：進む米中デカップリング、中国「保有米国債」の脅威減退か コラム：中国政府、株市場てこ入れ作戦に公的年金基金も動員 焦点：中国株、ＧＤＰ発表後も買い不発　不動産低迷で慎重ムード コラム：経済モデル転換目指す中国、不動産不況でも資源需要衰えず 焦点：ＳＨＥＩＮの香港上場、ＥＳＧ問題がなお影　投資家の懸念根強く 最終更新: 10/21(水) 19:08 ロイター

item.title: Elevance lifts 2026 profit forecast on disciplined cost management
item.description: Elevance Health on Wednesday raised its annual profit forecast after posting better-than-expected quarterly results, helped by lower medical costs.
item.dc:creator: Sneha K, Kamal Choudhury
item.content:encoded: Elevance Health (ELV.N) on Wednesday raised its annual profit forecast after posting better-than-expected quarterly results, helped by lower medical costs. Health insurers have been navigating declining membership, as well as rising costs in government-backed plans. Elevance, like other health insurers, has adjusted its pricing to reflect higher medical costs. For the third quarter, the company said higher premium yields and service fees offset lower membership, helping the company's insurance business post a $1.1 billion rise in revenue from a year earlier. Elevance forecast full-year adjusted profit to be at least $29 per share, compared with its previous outlook of at least $27 per share. Analysts on average estimate an annual profit of $27.23 per share, according to data compiled by LSEG. "Our earnings foundation is stronger, and we're entering 2027 with greater visibility and greater momentum," CEO Gail Boudreaux said in a conference call with analysts. For 2027, the company expects to deliver at least 12% growth in adjusted profit when compared to its earnings baseline of at least $26.75 per share. The company's adjusted quarterly profit was $6.99 per share, above expectations of $4.68 per share. Baird analyst Michael Ha said although Elevance delivered a large beat-and-raise, the smaller lift to recurring earnings leaves the stock vulnerable to a fade. Shares were down 1.3% in morning trading, after rising roughly 2% premarket post results. LOWER MEDICAL COSTS For the third quarter, the health insurer reported a medical loss ratio, the percentage of premiums spent on medical care, of 90.6%, better than analysts' expectations of 91.17%. The company said lower costs were due to better performance across its government-backed plans compared to the prior year. The company expects Medicaid margins to improve in 2027 as reimbursement rates become better aligned with elevated cost trends. Meanwhile, membership at its insurance unit declined by 487,000 compared with last year to about 44.9 million as of September 30, the company said. The company also named Jeff Park as president of Carelon, its health services business, effective December 1. "Carelon's pharmacy and services businesses are growing earnings while managing a larger share of the health plans' medical spending. That supports management's integrated strategy and helps offset pressure on insurance profits," said Daniel Barasa, portfolio manager at Gabelli Funds. The unit reported operating revenue of $19.3 billion, an increase of $1 billion from the prior year.

item.title: For Flavio Bolsonaro, runoff vote tests Brazilians' appetite for family's political brand
item.description: For right-wing Brazilian presidential candidate Flavio Bolsonaro, his biggest strength is also his greatest weakness: the Bolsonaro family name.
item.dc:creator: Luciana Novaes Magalhaes
item.content:encoded: For right-wing Brazilian presidential candidate Flavio Bolsonaro, his biggest strength is also his greatest weakness: the Bolsonaro family name. While supporters across Brazil consider him a more moderate iteration of his father's powerful conservative brand, many others view him as a continuation of Jair Bolsonaro's scorched-earth rule that polarized the nation and culminated in an [USN:S0N3UJ08N TEXT:"attempted coup"] after he lost the 2022 election. So far, more voters seem willing to test the first hypothesis, with Bolsonaro heading into Sunday's run-off as the [USN:S8N442025 TEXT:"frontrunner"] against incumbent President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva. A Bolsonaro victory would shift Brazil sharply rightward after four years of leftist rule, and likely push Latin America's largest nation closer into the orbit of the United States led by President [USN:S0N3ZY04Q TEXT:"Donald Trump"]. DISSATISFACTION WITH LULA Flavio's unexpected candidacy caught both insiders and markets off guard, especially since lingering corruption allegations — which he denies — and a crowded conservative field appeared to complicate his path to the presidency. But analysts say he has capitalized on growing [USN:L2N3QG01R TEXT:"dissatisfaction"] with 80-year-old Lula, while also tapping into his father's conservative coalition of powerful farmers, big business and evangelicals. Flavio, who is himself a converted evangelical, says that running for president felt like a calling after his father was sentenced to 27 years in prison for coup-plotting, a sentence he is now serving under house arrest. "I understand that everything happening is God's plan for our nation," [USN:L6N3XR02X TEXT:"he told Reuters"] late last year just after announcing his bid with his father's blessing. Murilo Miranda, a 42-year-old physician who attended a recent Bolsonaro rally in Sao Paulo, said Lula had overseen a system of welfare handouts and a bulging bureaucracy that had hindered Brazilian growth and led to endemic corruption. "They think the state is a father figure that is going to save them," Miranda told Reuters. Hermano Silveira, a 51-year-old contractor who was also at the rally, said Flavio was a new political force. "He is a young guy and we want change," Silveira said. RESOLVE HIS FATHER'S LEGAL PROBLEMS Bolsonaro has sought to acknowledge his father's missteps in power while tapping into his fervent base. During the first debate with Lula, he recognized his father's mishandled COVID-19 response, seeking to address a frequent line of attack. "Healthcare was not an area in which we achieved our best results under President Bolsonaro," he said. "I make this mea culpa here today." However, Bolsonaro has been clear that if he wins, he will quickly resolve his father's legal troubles. "I ask God for the opportunity to walk up the ramp of Planalto Palace next year alongside President Jair Messias Bolsonaro, so that he may place the presidential sash across my chest," he said on the campaign trail. So far, Bolsonaro has announced only one cabinet choice, naming Claudio Lottenberg, the former head of the private Albert Einstein hospital, as his pick for health minister. While promising to [USN:L1N4610Z9 TEXT:"cut spending"], Flavio has also pledged to boost public services and protect social welfare benefits for the population.

item.title: OpenAI president urges AI safeguards as group he funds opposes regulation
item.description: As OpenAI executives step up their public calls for federal AI safety rules, a political group the company’s president helped fund is spending millions to elect members of Congress who oppose restrictions on the technology.
item.dc:creator: Courtney Rozen
item.content:encoded: As OpenAI executives step up their public calls for federal AI safety rules, a political group the company’s president helped fund is spending millions to elect members of Congress who oppose restrictions on the technology. OpenAI’s safety practices have been in the spotlight in recent months, after the company said a swarm of its AI agents escaped containment and [USN:L6N44N119 TEXT:"hacked into the AI platform Hugging Face"]. OpenAI President Greg Brockman was among the group of six tech executives who later signed US [USN:L1N45K0VR TEXT:"President Donald Trump’s voluntary AI safety agreement"] on behalf of their companies, agreeing to work with "independent auditors" and to ensure their AI tools do not "hack or access technical systems in unintended ways." Yet Leading the Future, a political group backed with a $25 million donation from Brockman and his wife, Anna, opposes regulations that “unduly constrain or delay AI development” in the US. The group is spending millions to influence the outcome of at least 48 races for US House and Senate seats. INDUSTRY PROFITS VERSUS REGULATION Brockman’s backing prompted criticism from AI safety advocates, who say it raises questions about whether OpenAI executives genuinely want the US government to impose requirements on powerful AI systems. Federal government requirements could hurt the industry's profits if they slow the release of new models or prompt the companies to change how their products perform to address security concerns. OpenAI and rival Anthropic are [USN:L1N4610T9 TEXT:"laying the groundwork for public offerings"] that are expected to rank among the largest ever. “There are leaders in industry who want to pay lip service to regulation because they realize where public opinion is,” said Charlie Blaettler of Guardrails Alliance, a political group formed to counter Leading the Future. “But they're the same leaders who stood up a super PAC whose sole purpose was to oppose candidates who stand up for regulation.” OpenAI said in a blog post that the Brockmans' donation was in a personal capacity, not on behalf of the company. Greg Brockman's personal spokesperson declined to comment on his donations. In a post on X from 2025, Brockman said that "being pro-AI does not mean being anti-regulation. It means being thoughtful." Leading the Future’s spokesperson, Jesse Hunt, did not address the donation in a statement, saying the group seeks "champions who can work together in Congress to advance a strong, responsible national regulatory AI framework." The New York Times reported in September that the Brockmans backed out of a pledge to donate another $25 million to Leading the Future. Leading the Future declined to comment on the New York Times' reporting. FEDERAL LAW TO PRE-EMPT STATE AI LAWS Other contributors to Leading the Future include Marc Andreessen and Ben Horowitz, who, along with their venture capital firm Andreessen Horowitz, gave a combined $50 million to the group, according to Federal Election Commission records. Andreessen Horowitz is an investor in OpenAI. One of the candidates Leading the Future is backing is Republican Andy Barr, who is running to represent Kentucky in the Senate. Barr told the newspaper the Lexington Herald-Leader in March that he supports federal legislation that would block individual states from passing or enforcing their own regulations on AI, a concept known as pre-emption. Build American AI, a nonprofit group affiliated with Leading the Future, has run advertisements on social media platforms calling on Congress to pass a national standard for AI, rather than allowing states to pass their own rules. Leading the Future also sent funds to Republicans Julia Letlow, who is running for Senate in Louisiana, and Amanda McKinney, a candidate for Congress in Washington state. Both say on their campaign websites that they are opposed to "heavy-handed" regulation of the AI sector. OpenAI rival Anthropic has [USN:L6N43N198 TEXT:"given at least $40 million"] to Public First Action, a political action committee that is against federal pre-emption laws. Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei has called federal pre-emption of state rules [USN:L3N3S80QH TEXT:""too blunt""].

item.description: BRUSSELS, Oct 21 : EU tech regulators will investigate whether online hotel reservation website Booking.com is doing enough to weed out fraudulent listings and phishing scams to comply with EU online content rules, the European Commission said on Wednesday.The Commission, which is the EU tech and competition

Booking.com targeted in EU investigation into phishing scams, fraudulent listings

FAST

BRUSSELS, Oct 21 : EU tech regulators will investigate whether online hotel reservation website Booking.com is doing enough to weed out fraudulent listings and phishing scams to comply with EU online content rules, the European Commission said on Wednesday. The Commission, which is the EU tech and competition enforcer, said it opened an investigation following a preliminary probe and after analysing risk assessment reports submitted by Booking.com this year and the previous three years. Big online platforms are required to do more to tackle illegal and harmful content on their sites under the bloc's Digital Services Act, or risk fines of as much as 6 per cent of their global annual turnover for violations. Booking.com said it was engaging constructively with the Commission. "Security, trust and the protection of personal information are top priorities at Booking.com," a spokesperson for the company said.

"We remain committed to working with relevant governments, regulators, law enforcement and industry partners to combat cybercrime and online fraud, and protect travelers and partners." The EU investigation will focus on fake listings — such as for non-existent properties — impersonation fraud and non-compliant accommodation offers, and whether Booking.com has properly identified, assessed and mitigated the systemic risks related to these. Regulators will also look into phishing scams exploiting Booking.com's reservation and guest data shared with accommodation providers, the Commission said. A third element will be paid-for boosted listings not clearly identifiable as advertisements. Booking.com is part of Booking Holdings. "Europeans should be able to book their holidays without fear of being scammed," EU tech chief Henna Virkkunen said in a statement. "The Digital Services Act sets clear responsibilities on platforms to address these risks, and we must ensure that the leading booking platform in Europe takes those responsibilities seriously," she said.

Source: Reuters

item.title: 中国奇瑞、米自動車メーカーとの提携に前向き＝幹部
item.description: [蕪湖（中国） ２１日 ロイター] - 中国の自動車大手、奇瑞汽車（チェリー）の幹部は２１日、米自動車メーカーとの提...
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
中国奇瑞、米自動車メーカーとの提携に前向き＝幹部 10/21 19:02 配信

2026年10月12日、パリのオートショーに展示された奇瑞汽車（チェリー）の車。 REUTERS/Benoit Tessier

[蕪湖（中国） ２１日 ロイター] - 中国の自動車大手、奇瑞汽車（チェリー）の幹部は２１日、米自動車メーカーとの提携に前向きな姿勢を示した。「オモダ」「ジェクー」ブランドを展開する同社は欧州などで急成長しており、今後は北米での事業拡大を目指す。

バイスプレジデントのチャーリー・チャン氏は中国東部・蕪湖の本社でインタビューに応じ、２０２７年初めにカナダでブランドを立ち上げる準備を進めていることも明らかにした。

米国では１００％を超える関税やデータセキュリティー規制が障壁となり、中国の自動車メーカーは事実上締め出されている。

チャン氏は「米国については当然さまざまな選択肢を探っている」と述べ、柔軟に対応する姿勢を強調した。「米自動車メーカーとの提携の可能性も含め、さまざまな選択肢に非常に前向きだ」と語った。具体的にどのような提携を想定しているかは明らかにしなかった。

「技術面ではハードウエアもソフトウエアも中国製に頼らない方法を確実に見いだせる」と述べ、米国市場への参入に道筋をつけられるとの自信を示した。

ロイター 関連ニュース 焦点：トヨタの中国合弁2社に再編機運、市場縮小と競争激化で転換点 焦点：テスラ、ロボタクシー「サイバーキャブ」で試す規制の限界 焦点：中国車メーカー、カナダ進出に本腰　米市場開放にらみ「予行演習」 コラム：中国車の米市場参入は時間の問題 アングル：中国自動車メーカーが欧州で最も勢力を伸ばした地域 最終更新: 10/21(水) 19:02 ロイター

item.title: Putin hosts Trump envoy for new Ukraine peace talks, frees US citizen held in Russia
item.description: Stephen Hubbard, a 74-year-old retired US school teacher who had been held in Russia on mercenary charges, has been released.
item.dc:creator: CNA
item.content:encoded:
Advertisement

Putin hosts Trump envoy for new Ukraine peace talks, frees US citizen held in Russia

Stephen Hubbard, a 74-year-old retired US school teacher who had been held in Russia on mercenary charges, has been released.

Russian presidential envoy Kirill Dmitriev greets US special envoy Steve Witkoff upon his arrival at Pulkovo Airport in Saint Petersburg, Russia on Oct 21, 2026. (Photo: Reuters)

FAST

ST PETERSBURG, Russia: President Vladimir Putin hosted US Special Envoy Steve Witkoff in a grand imperial palace on Wednesday (Oct 21) to review new ideas on ending the war in Ukraine amid Washington's latest push to stop Europe's bloodiest conflict since World War Two. The talks in St Petersburg , the ninth time that Witkoff has met Putin in person, began with a goodwill gesture from Russia - the release of a retired US school teacher held in Russia. The encounter comes amid concerns in Kyiv and among its allies that the United States is backing away from Ukraine, at times holding back real-time intelligence on Russian attacks and hobbling Ukraine's military communications. The latest talks came more than two years since US President Donald Trump promised in his successful election campaign to end the Ukraine war within 24 hours.

Witkoff flew into Russia's second city on Wednesday morning a day after conducting what a US official called "constructive" talks in Oslo with Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy, the leaders of Finland and Norway and European and NATO representatives, as President Donald Trump said it was time for Ukraine to end the war or face "a very bad thing." US-Ukraine ties have deteriorated sharply since Trump announced a diesel export deal with Russia earlier this month to help lower prices in the United States. High fuel costs since he launched strikes on Iran have hurt his Republicans ahead of November legislative elections. Since the diesel deal, Ukraine has complained of disruption to some intelligence sharing and to its use of the Starshield military satellite system , though Zelenskyy said that Tuesday's Oslo meeting had reached an agreement to resolve those issues.

Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy meets US Special Envoy Steve Witkoff, Norwegian Prime Minister Jonas Gahr Store and Finnish President Alexander Stubb in Oslo, Norway on Oct 20, 2026. (Photo: Reuters/NTB/Heiko Junge)

STARLINK SPEEDS Citing US officials and people familiar with the matter, the Wall Street Journal reported on Wednesday that billionaire Elon Musk had last week ordered the slowdown of a military-grade version of SpaceX's Starlink satellite service that Ukraine relies on to track Russian ballistic missile strikes. Reuters could not immediately verify the report. Musk has said any such decision is taken by the US military or the president. Trump has said he was not responsible. US Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth said on Tuesday that the problem lay with the terms of service Kyiv needed to comply with. US Secretary of State Marco Rubio said on Wednesday that Witkoff's meeting with Zelenskyy was positive and that Witkoff would share the results with Russia. He also reiterated that Washington had not pulled back Kyiv's ability to access Starlink. "He will now, armed with those ideas, be able to go to St Petersburg and share them with the Russian side, and let's see if we can make some progress," he said.

Related:

Zelenskyy hails resumption of US advance warning of strikes on Ukraine

Ukraine claims US missile holdup ahead of reported talks

TRUMP PRESSURE Despite the apparently cordial nature of Tuesday's meeting in Oslo, Trump, as he showed in comments in the White House on Tuesday, remains frustrated with Zelenskyy, whom he has repeatedly rebuked and suggested needs to be replaced. "He's going to have to want to make a deal, because I don't think his people are going to stand for it any longer," Trump told reporters on the eve of the talks in Russia. Putin, who has shown few signs of compromising on his central war aims, which include full Russian control of the Donetsk region in eastern Ukraine and no NATO membership for Kyiv, will receive Witkoff in the Constantine Palace, a grand imperial edifice in what is the Kremlin chief's home city. Kirill Dmitriev, Putin's special investment envoy and his main point man for potential economic and financial deals with the US, would also be present at the meeting with Witkoff, Kremlin aide Yuri Ushakov said. A US official said Ukraine had brought new ideas and proposals to the Oslo talks, which had made "meaningful progress" toward a coordinated approach to engaging with Russia. The official, who spoke on the condition of anonymity, said the talks covered "key elements of a comprehensive peace framework", including security guarantees for Ukraine, a post-war economic plan and a broader European security architecture. Witkoff would aim to "create a pathway toward direct trilateral and broader multilateral negotiations," the official said. Zelenskyysaid he hoped to discuss key issues on how to end the war during a trilateral meeting with Putin and Trump. The Kremlin has repeatedly said that any Putin-Zelenskyy meeting would need to be painstakingly prepared in advance by aides to make it worthwhile and that a lot of the legwork required for an overall agreement would need to be in place. Trump said on Tuesday he had raised the idea with Putin of freeing Stephen Hubbard - a 74-year-old retired US school teacher being held in Russia on mercenary charges he denies. Putin told Witkoff that Hubbard was at the airport waiting to fly back to the United States with him. Witkoff thanked Putin for the goodwill gesture. Hubbard was first detained in April 2022 and was later sentenced to six years and 10 months on charges whose veracity his family and US-based lawyer question.

Source: Reuters/nh

item.title: Who is Stephen Hubbard, the US citizen released by Russia?
item.description: Here are details of Hubbard's case.
item.dc:creator: Lucy Papachristou
item.content:encoded: President Vladimir Putin announced the release of American citizen Stephen Hubbard from Russian detention on Wednesday, [USN:L6N4670LA TEXT:"at the start of talks"] with US special envoy Steve Witkoff. Here are details of Hubbard's case: WHO IS STEPHEN HUBBARD? Hubbard, 74, a retired schoolteacher, grew up in Big Rapids, Michigan, and served in the US Air Force and National Guard, according to military records cited by the New York Times. He earned a master’s degree in English and lived in Japan for 25 years where he taught English before moving to Cyprus and then, in 2014, to Izyum in eastern Ukraine with a Ukrainian partner, according to his sister, Patricia Hubbard Fox. Fox told Reuters in 2024 that Hubbard subsisted on a pension of about $300 a month and had few connections with local people. The siblings last spoke in September 2021. HOW WAS HE CAPTURED? Russia launched its full-scale war in Ukraine in February 2022 and captured Izyum two months later. Ukrainian forces retook the city in September 2022, but Hubbard was already in Russian custody by then. Russian state media said Hubbard had been detained in April 2022 and alleged he had been manning a Ukrainian military checkpoint. Reuters could not independently establish the circumstances of his capture. Fox said she recognised her brother in a YouTube video showing a man being questioned about his views on Putin and the war. Another video showed him with his hands bound, being struck with a sandal. Reuters could not verify when or where the videos were recorded. WHY WAS HE IMPRISONED? Following a closed trial, a Moscow court convicted Hubbard of being a mercenary in October 2024 and sentenced him to six years and 10 months in prison.Prosecutors said Hubbard had joined a Ukrainian territorial defence unit, received training, weapons and ammunition, and was promised $1,000 a month. Russian state media said he had pleaded guilty to the charges he faced. Fox questioned the reported confession, however, saying Hubbard held pro-Russian views and was unlikely to have taken up arms in his seventies. Martin De Luca, his US-based lawyer, told Reuters in June 2025 that Hubbard had told him the charges against him were false and that he was not in any combat or military unit. He cited Hubbard as telling him Russian soldiers had simply grabbed him from his house. WHAT IS HUBBARD'S CURRENT STATUS? In January 2025, Washington designated Hubbard as wrongfully detained, enabling the US government to pursue negotiations for his release. The State Department has said Russia refused to grant US officials consular access. The New York Times reported in February 2025 that Hubbard had been moved through at least five Russian detention centres before his trial. His lawyer said Hubbard's legal team found out only in April 2025 that he was being held in a facility in the Mordovia region, east of Moscow.

item.title: イラク、イランとの国境検問所を閉鎖 治安状況確認中＝関係筋
item.description: [バスラ ２１日 ロイター] -
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
[バスラ ２１日 ロイター] - イラクの国境当局者は２１日、イランとの国境にある交通量の多いシーブ検問所を閉鎖し、治安状況の評価や、禁止物品の密輸を阻止するための検査装置の設置を行っていると述べた。

同検問所の他の関係筋２人によると、追って通知があるまで、乗客、車両、商用トラックの通行が禁止される。

イラクは９月、サウジアラビアに対するドローン（無人機）攻撃を受けた予防措置として、イランとのもう一つの国境検問所であるシャラムチェの閉鎖を命令。サウジ当局は、ドローンがイラクから発射されたと主張していた。

イラクの国境検問所当局者はロイターに対し、シーブ検問所における現在の治安対策は脆弱で不十分だと語った。

item.title: Gobierno de Colombia fijará por decreto presupuesto para 2027 por error de trámite en el Congreso
item.description: El Gobierno de Colombia fijará por decreto el presupuesto de gastos para 2027 por 634,9 billones de pesos (200.679 millones de dólares), después de que el proyecto de ley aprobado por el Congreso se hundió por un vicio de trámite, anunció el miércoles el vicepresidente, José Manuel Restrepo.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: El Gobierno de Colombia fijará por decreto el presupuesto de gastos para 2027 por 634,9 billones de pesos (200.679 millones de dólares), después de que el proyecto de ley aprobado por el Congreso se hundió por un vicio de trámite, anunció el miércoles el vicepresidente, José Manuel Restrepo. La cifra total, que supera los 555,8 billones de pesos del presupuesto vigente para 2026, no cambiará frente a la aprobada por el Congreso. "El Gobierno Nacional, en el día de hoy, procederá a decretar dicho Presupuesto General de la Nación", dijo Restrepo en una declaración, al destacar que incluye todos los gastos sociales y de funcionamiento del Estado. El presupuesto prevé un déficit fiscal récord de 9,4% del Producto Interno Bruto (PIB), en medio de fuertes necesidades de financiamiento, que incluso llevaron al presidente Abelardo De La Espriella a buscar apoyo del Fondo Monetario Internacional. El Senado aprobó el proyecto de ley de presupuesto el lunes en la noche con 57 votos a favor y uno en contra, mientras que la Cámara de Representantes lo hizo el martes en la madrugada con 112 votos a favor y uno en contra. Uno de los artículos del presupuesto fue aprobado en la Cámara de Representantes con un contenido diferente al del Senado, lo que, según congresistas, vició todo el trámite del proyecto de ley. Al ser aprobados textos diferentes, debió darse una conciliación entre la Cámara y el Senado, trámite que no se realizó antes de la fecha límite del 20 de octubre. "Regirá el proyecto que el Gobierno presentó con las modificaciones aprobadas y discutidas por el Congreso en el primer debate", aseguró el vicepresidente. "Tanto el monto de 634,9 billones de pesos, como la distribución que el Congreso estudió y aprobó en primer debate, quedaron aprobados, así como también las facultades de traslado y de reorientación presupuestal", explicó el funcionario. El presupuesto que había sido aprobado por el Senado y la Cámara de Representantes contemplaba una reasignación de recursos entre diferentes sectores, con recortes en rubros relacionados con el acuerdo de paz e incrementos en los recursos para el pago del servicio de la deuda y para salud. Al hundirse el proyecto, esa reasignación no se aplicará, según congresistas. Con el proyecto presentado por el Gobierno, el recorte al presupuesto de funcionamiento de la Jurisdicción Especial para la Paz (JEP), creada en virtud del acuerdo de paz de 2016 firmado con la antigua guerrilla de las Fuerzas Armadas Revolucionarias de Colombia (FARC), será menor que el propuesto, según legisladores. Restrepo envió un mensaje de tranquilidad a los inversionistas, tenedores de bonos y a la comunidad financiera internacional y aseguró que el presupuesto recoge el esfuerzo de ajuste fiscal que necesita el país. El vicepresidente anunció que próximamente se presentará al Congreso la "Ley de Rescate" para organizar las finanzas publicas y garantizar el crecimiento de la economía. (1 dólar = 3.163,76 pesos)

Kentaro Okasaka

item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
ラピダス、2ナノ量産「ほぼ計画通り」　当初の顧客は米中心に＝会長 10/21 18:42 配信

ラピダスのロゴ。2026年8月21日、都内で撮影。REUTERS/Issei Kato/File Photo

Kentaro Okasaka

[東京 ２１日 ロイター] - ラピダス（東京都千代田区）の東哲郎会長は ２１日、来年後半の量産を目指す回路線幅２ナノメートル（ナノは１０億分の１）の半導体について、量産に向け「ほぼオンスケジュール」で進んでいると述べた。課題となる顧客獲得に関し、当初は人工知能（ＡＩ）関連の需要がある米国が中心になるとの見通しを示した。

都内で講演し、来場者との質疑で語った。日本国内でも、コンピューター関連企業などへの半導体提供に向けた協議が進展しているとした。その上で「今後、非常にマーケットが広がっていくので、それほど心配していない」と話した。

また、ラピダスの工場がある北海道千歳市に関し、台湾積体電路製造（ＴＳＭＣ）が進出した熊本県を念頭に「九州を真似するわけではないが、サイエンスパークのようなものを形成していこうということで非常に活発に動いていて、われわれも一緒にやっていこうと考えている」と語った。

item.description: [台北 ２１日 ロイター] - 台湾の公平交易委員会（公正取引委員会）は２１日、競争上の懸念を理由に、シンガポール...
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
グラブのフードパンダ台湾事業買収、当局が認めず　競争懸念で 10/21 18:36 配信

配車・配達サービス会社グラブのロゴ。2026年2月25日、シンガポールで撮影。 REUTERS/Edgar Su

[台北 ２１日 ロイター] - 台湾の公平交易委員会（公正取引委員会）は２１日、競争上の懸念を理由に、シンガポールのグラブによるフードパンダの台湾宅配事業買収を認めなかったと発表した。

東南アジア最大の配車・配達サービス会社グラブは３月、フードパンダの台湾宅配事業を現金６億ドルで買収すると発表していた。グラブにとって東南アジア域外への初進出となる計画だった。

公平交易委員会は、買収によって生じる競争への悪影響が経済全体への利益を上回ると判断した。フードパンダを傘下に置く独料理宅配デリバリーヒーローとグラブの両社が確約した条件についても「競争上の懸念を解消するには不十分」とした。

item.title: Netflix's ad stumble deepens fears its growth is hitting a wall
item.description: Netflix's cut to its advertising sales forecast is fuelling concerns that its growth engine is losing steam, threatening the edge that made it a model for the media industry.
item.dc:creator: Aditya Soni, Kanishka Ajmera
item.content:encoded: Netflix's (NFLX.O) cut to its advertising sales forecast is fuelling concerns that its growth engine is losing steam, threatening the edge that made it a model for the media industry. Shares of the company fell nearly 5% in Wednesday afternoon trading after Netflix forecast a fourth consecutive quarter of slowing revenue growth, as one of Hollywood's biggest spenders on original content struggles to deliver major hits. "Netflix is increasingly being judged against its own exceptionally high standards, raising questions about whether it has lost some of the focus and agility that once distinguished it from rivals," PP Foresight analyst Paolo Pescatore wrote in a client note. The stock has lost about a quarter of its value this year, with Netflix's failed pursuit of Warner Bros Discovery adding to concerns that it is running out of avenues for growth beyond price increases and its crackdown on password sharing. Netflix's advertising business, long seen as a key source of future growth, is expanding more slowly than expected, while its push into gaming, backed by deals including one to add some "Grand Theft Auto" titles, has yet to make a meaningful contribution. Meanwhile, YouTube and TikTok are competing for viewers with a steady stream of relatively inexpensive user-generated content, while the combination of Warner Bros Discovery and Paramount under Skydance is set to intensify competition. Netflix has responded by cutting 6% of its workforce and replacing two top programming executives. Co-CEO Ted Sarandos said on Tuesday that the moves would allow Netflix to focus on its core business of producing TV shows and films aimed at making the service a must-have for consumers. Some analysts said incoming content chief Peter Rice will help improve Netflix's film and television slate by sharpening its focus on prestige programming and drawing on his relationships with top creative talent. "His industry relationships could prove valuable in attracting and retaining top filmmakers, especially following the departures of creators such as the Duffer Brothers, Shawn Levy, and Noah Baumbach," Citizens analyst Matthew Condon said. "Rice’s extensive experience overseeing live sports could support a more ambitious approach to premium sports programming, further enhancing Netflix’s value proposition." ANALYSTS CUT BACK EXPECTATIONS More than 20 brokerages have cut their price targets on the stock following the results, according to LSEG data. If current losses hold, the streaming giant is on track to lose about $13 billion in market value. BofA Global Research analysts said the leadership change and layoffs were "a signal that management is focused on improving content output and creative hit rates." Netflix trades at nearly 18.3 times expected earnings over the next 12 months, compared with 14.76 times for Walt Disney (DIS.N) and 6.26 times for Comcast (CMCSA.O) .

item.description: [フランクフルト ２１日 ロイター] - 欧州中央銀行（ＥＣＢ）のエコノミストらは２１日のブログで、ユーロ圏経済は今...
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
ユーロ圏、ＡＩとグリーン経済がエネショック緩和＝ＥＣＢブログ 10/21 18:28 配信

[フランクフルト ２１日 ロイター] - 欧州中央銀行（ＥＣＢ）のエコノミストらは２１日のブログで、ユーロ圏経済は今年のエネルギーショックを予想以上にうまく乗り切っており、化石燃料への依存度低下、財政支援強化、そしてＡＩ（人工知能）投資ブームが成長の維持に寄与していると述べた。

域内経済について、現在の石油依存度は１９９０年代初頭に比べて約半分に低下しており、エネルギー価格ショックの影響が限定的になっていると推定。ＡＩ関連の貿易がユーロ圏にとって「重要な追い風」となっており、技術関連の輸出受注やＡＩ関連セクターが好調に推移していると指摘した。

一方で、財政刺激策といった支援の多くが一時的なものにとどまる可能性があると警告。世界的な需要、財政刺激策、ＡＩ投資が後退すれば、地政学的緊張が悪化したり、エネルギー市場で新たな混乱が生じたりした場合、ユーロ圏は脆弱な立場に置かれることになる。

item.title: Putin agrees to resume 3-way peace talks with Ukraine and US
item.description: Russian President Vladimir Putin has agreed to resume US-mediated peace talks with Ukraine as soon as next month, the Kremlin said on Wednesday, after Putin met US envoy Steve Witkoff in Washington's latest push to stop Europe's bloodiest conflict since World War Two.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Russian President Vladimir Putin has agreed to resume US-mediated peace talks with Ukraine as soon as next month, the Kremlin said on Wednesday, after Putin met US envoy Steve Witkoff in Washington's latest push to stop Europe's bloodiest conflict since World War Two. The negotiations in a grand imperial palace in St Petersburg, the ninth time that Witkoff has met Putin in person, began with a goodwill gesture from Russia - the release of [USN:L8N4670PP TEXT:"Stephen Hubbard, a retired US school teacher"] held in Russia whom US President Trump had asked the Kremlin chief to release. Wednesday's encounter unfolded amid concerns in Kyiv and among its allies that the United States is backing away from Ukraine, at times holding back real-time intelligence on Russian attacks and hobbling Ukraine's military communications. The latest talks also came more than two years since Trump promised in his successful election campaign to end the Ukraine war within 24 hours. The Kremlin said the new 3-way peace talks, which would be at a technical level, could take place in Abu Dhabi and would be focused on how to guarantee the security of Ukraine and Russia once the war ended. They could begin sometime on or after November 10, it said. The last US-mediated peace talks took place in February before the United States and Israel launched a war against Iran . The Kremlin was less upbeat, however, about the outcome of talks Witkoff had held a day earlier in Oslo with Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskiy, the leaders of Finland and Norway, and European and NATO representatives. Witkoff told Putin the talks had been characterised by "some degree of momentum" and a US official said Ukraine had brought [USN:L1N466099 TEXT:"new ideas and proposals"]. "These nuances, so to speak, do not entirely satisfy us," Kremlin aide Yuri Ushakov told reporters after the St Petersburg meeting - which lasted nearly three hours. POSSIBLE MEETING BETWEEN TRUMP, PUTIN AND XI Ukraine and Russia remain far apart when it comes to the terms of any possible peace deal, though Trump has recently intensified pressure on Ukraine to strike some kind of a deal. He said on Tuesday it was time for Ukraine to end the war or face "a very bad thing." Putin also used Wednesday's talks to offer to help Trump deal with Iran, saying Russia had a decades-long relationship with Tehran which it has repeatedly offered to leverage to address US concerns about Iran's nuclear programme. Putin told Witkoff it was possible and necessary to get a deal with Tehran, the Kremlin said. Russia could also supply vast quantities of fertiliser to the United States to help US farmers, the Russian president told Witkoff. [USN:L1N4650BJ TEXT:"A potential meeting in China next month"] with Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping was also discussed. The Kremlin said Beijing was already preparing what it said would be the first meeting of its kind in history. 'NEW IDEAS' Putin has shown few signs of compromising on his central war aims, which include full Russian control of the Donetsk region in eastern Ukraine, no NATO membership for Kyiv, and an overall peace deal rather than a temporary ceasefire. Kirill Dmitriev, Putin's special investment envoy, was also present at the talks with Witkoff and the Kremlin said that major joint economic projects had been discussed, including some that were close to being realised. Witkoff said he had brought some documents with him containing various ideas for a potential peace deal for Putin to review, and that Jared Kushner, Trump's son-in-law, also wanted to convey some ideas to Putin. Kushner later joined the meeting remotely by phone. Zelenskiy said he [USN:L1N4670EW TEXT:"hoped to discuss key issues"] on how to end the war during a trilateral meeting with Putin and Trump. The Kremlin has repeatedly said that any Putin-Zelenskiy meeting would need to be painstakingly prepared in advance by aides to make it worthwhile. FRAYING US-UKRAINE TIES US-Ukraine ties have deteriorated sharply since Trump announced a diesel export deal with Russia earlier this month to help lower prices in the United States. High fuel costs since he launched strikes on Iran have hurt his Republicans ahead of November legislative elections. Since the diesel deal, Ukraine has complained of disruption to some intelligence sharing and to its use of the Starshield military satellite system, though Zelenskiy said that Tuesday's Oslo meeting had reached an agreement to resolve those issues. Citing US officials and people familiar with the matter, the Wall Street Journal reported on Wednesday that billionaire Elon Musk had last week ordered the slowdown of a military-grade version of SpaceX's Starlink satellite service that Ukraine relies on to track Russian ballistic missile strikes. Reuters could not immediately verify the report. Musk has said any such decision is taken by the US military or the president. Trump has said he was not responsible and US Secretary of State Marco Rubio reiterated on Wednesday that Washington had not pulled back Kyiv's ability to access Starlink.

item.title: 豪データセンターＮＥＸＴＤＣ、新規開発凍結 時価総額ほぼ半減
item.description:
Scott Murdoch Rajasik Mukherjee
[シドニー ２１日 ロイター] - オーストラリアのデ...
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
豪データセンターＮＥＸＴＤＣ、新規開発凍結　時価総額ほぼ半減 10/21 18:15 配信

データセンター運営会社ＮＥＸＴＤＣのロゴ。2026年6月22日、シドニーで撮影。 REUTERS/Hollie Adams

Scott Murdoch　Rajasik Mukherjee

[シドニー ２１日 ロイター] - オーストラリアのデータセンター運営会社ＮＥＸＴＤＣの株価が２１日急落し、時価総額がほぼ半減した。今後１年間の売上高見通しを大幅に引き下げ、開発計画を凍結すると発表したことが響いた。

同社によると、メルボルンの主要プロジェクトの一つで電力網の増強が遅れており、今年度に計上する予定だった売上高約１億４０００万豪ドル（９８００万米ドル）が先送りされる。ＮＥＸＴＤＣは当面、新規開発プロジェクトと用地取得を全て凍結すると説明した。

株価は４１．７％安で取引を終え、時価総額が約３０億豪ドル減少した。

人工知能（ＡＩ）に対する投資家心理はここ数週間で悪化している。急増する計算処理や用地、電力のコストに見合う成果を生むのかを巡り、巨額のＡＩ投資に疑問が広がっている。オーストラリアでは先週、データセンター企業が新規株式公開（ＩＰＯ）を撤回した。データセンター株やハイテク株が売られ、クレジット投資家はＡＩ関連企業への投資を一段と厳しく選別するようになっている。

ＮＥＸＴＤＣは２０２７年の純売上高を４億７５００万─５億豪ドルと見込む。従来予想の６億１５００万─６億４０００万豪ドルから引き下げた。調整後ＥＢＩＴＤＡ（利払い・税金・償却前利益）予想も、３億８５００万─４億１０００万豪ドルから２億４５００万─２億６５００万豪ドルに引き下げた。いずれも電力網増強の遅れで影響を受ける契約分を除いた数字だ。

同社によると、配電会社ジェメナ・エレクトリシティ・ネットワークスによる工事の遅れで、メルボルンのＭ３データセンターへの次の電力供給拡大は２０２８年になる見通しだ。

ジェメナは地域住民や関係者の反対を受け、Ｍ３への電力供給の増強に必要な電力網工事の一部を中断している。再開は早くても２７年２月になるとみている。

FAST

TAIPEI: Taiwan's Fair Trade Commission said on Wednesday (Oct 21) it had blocked Grab's purchase of Delivery Hero's Foodpanda delivery business in Taiwan, citing competition concerns. Grab, Southeast Asia's biggest ride-hailing and delivery firm, said in March it would pay US$600 million in cash for the Foodpanda delivery business in Taiwan, in its first expansion outside the region. The Fair Trade Commission said the harm to competition from the proposed deal outweighed its overall economic benefits, and that the commitments offered by the companies were "insufficient to eliminate the competition concerns". Grab said it was disappointed by the decision.  "Grab's core business across Southeast Asia remains robust. We will continue to focus our capital and resources on executing our growth roadmap and empowering communities across our regional footprint." Delivery Hero said in a statement that under the terms of the transaction, it has appropriate deal protections, including a break fee arrangement, subject to certain conditions.

Source: Reuters/nh

インフロニアＨＤ、新株発行価格を2179.5円に決定 10/21 17:56 配信

［東京　２１日　ロイター］ - インフロニア・ホールディングスは２１日、新株発行・売出価格を１株２１７９．５円に決めたと発表した。同日の株価終値２２４７円から３％の割引率とした。
